chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Allah Mighty and Majestic has not been disobeyed by anything more severe than drinking wine; indeed, one of them (the drinker) would neglect the obligatory prayer and leap upon his mother, his sister, and his daughter, while he is not fully conscious (of what he is doing).

key_terms.لَا يَعْقِلُ: Does not have intellect / is not fully conscious

ai.seo_question: What are the primary spiritual and social consequences of drinking wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes wine as the 'gateway' to sin, illustrating how intoxication erodes rational faculty (aql), leading to the neglect of core duties like obligatory prayer and causing impulsive transgressions against female kin. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that khamr is not merely a physical intoxicant but a spiritual veil that obscures divine consciousness and social order.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has not been disobeyed by a thing more severe than drinking of the wine, as one of them (drinkers) would neglect the Prayer, and leap upon his mother, and his sister, and his daughter, and he has no intellect (for it)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from his father who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah is not disobeyed by anything more severely than by drinking wine. One of them may neglect obligatory Salat (prayer), fall on his mother, sister or daughter when drunk and be devoid of reason.’”
